topic: Google Sheets/Docs/Drive as a non-technical CMS for a static academic site: real API limits, verified endpoint behaviour, image pipeline, build/publish triggers, schema validation, and an honest comparison against Notion/Airtable/Decap/Sveltia/Tina/Keystatic/Sanity/Contentful/Payload/plain-Markdown.
key_findings: VERIFIED LIVE (curl, 2026-09-04): the legacy gviz endpoint still works. `https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/{ID}/gviz/tq?tqx=out:json&headers=1&gid=0` returns HTTP 200 with a JSONP body prefixed `/*O_o*/\ngoogle.visualization.Query.setResponse({...});`. It also serves CSV via `tqx=out:csv` and supports the Google Visualization Query Language via `&tq=select A,B limit 2`. Its CORS header echoes the request Origin (`access-control-allow-origin: https://satishregonda.in`), so it is browser-fetchable. BUT the `google/google-visualization-issues` repo was ARCHIVED by Google on 2026-04-18 — the API is unsupported, not merely undocumented.

THE SINGLE MOST DANGEROUS FINDING, verified live: gviz FAILS SILENTLY on a bad tab name. `...gviz/tq?tqx=out:json&sheet=NoSuchTab` returns HTTP 200 with `"status":"ok"` and the response signature (`sig:1418075960`) is IDENTICAL to the no-`sheet`-param request — i.e. it silently falls back to the first sheet. If the professor renames 'Publications' to 'Publications 2026', the build succeeds and quietly publishes the wrong tab's data. The official Sheets API v4 returns a hard 400 for a bad range instead. This alone disqualifies gviz as the primary read path.

Google Sheets API v4 official quotas: 300 read requests/min per project AND 60 read requests/min per user per project (same for writes). No daily cap. 2 MB recommended max payload; requests >180s error; 429 on exceed. CRITICAL: the limits page now states that exceeding quota is "planned to incur charges to your Google Cloud billing account later in 2026" — Sheets API is free today but is being moved onto billing. At our scale (one `values.batchGet` per build, ~100 builds/month) this is ~0.003% of quota and will remain free-tier, but it must be budgeted for.

Google OAuth scope classification is the decisive auth argument: `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/spreadsheets.readonly` is a SENSITIVE scope (requires Google app verification) and `drive.readonly` is a RESTRICTED scope (requires restricted-scope verification PLUS a third-party security assessment). A service account sidesteps both entirely — no consent screen, no verification, no annual re-review. Use a service account with the sheet and the image folder shared read-only to its `...@....iam.gserviceaccount.com` address.

VERIFIED LIVE: Sheets API v4 with no credentials returns `403 PERMISSION_DENIED — "Method doesn't allow unregistered callers (callers without established identity). Please use API Key or other form of API consumer identity to call this API."` So an API key IS required even for a world-readable sheet — but an API key alone works for read-only on a link-shared sheet, no OAuth needed.

VERIFIED LIVE: `https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/{ID}/export?format=csv&gid={GID}` issues a 307 redirect, then returns `200 text/csv`, `access-control-allow-origin: *`, `content-disposition: attachment`, and crucially `cache-control: no-cache, no-store, max-age=0, must-revalidate`. Same no-cache header on gviz. By contrast the 'Publish to web' 2PACX URL (`/spreadsheets/d/e/2PACX-.../pub?gid=0&single=true&output=csv`) IS cached by Google and goes stale for minutes — Harry Cresswell's Hugo write-up documents needing a SHA256-of-timestamp cache-buster query param to force freshness. Never use 2PACX for a build source.

VERIFIED LIVE: the modern Drive image URL is a redirect, not a real endpoint. `https://drive.google.com/thumbnail?id={ID}&sz=w1000` returns `302 → https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/d/{ID}=w1000`. The `sz=w1000` param becomes the `=w1000` suffix on lh3. The classic `drive.google.com/uc?export=view&id={ID}` broke in January 2024 (GitHub community discussion #86986 — GitHub Pages sites lost all Drive images overnight, no user error). Neither endpoint is contractual; both are rate-limited by Google's image infra and return 429 under load.

Drive's worst failure mode is `downloadQuotaExceeded`: HTTP 403, domain `usageLimits`, reason `downloadQuotaExceeded`, message "The download quota for this file has been exceeded." It fires on rapid repeated programmatic access to a single file, is undocumented as to threshold, lasts a community-reported 10–30 minutes, and affects service accounts identically to user accounts. This is a hard argument for downloading images ONCE at build time into a content-addressed cache, never hot-linking and never re-fetching unchanged files.

Drive API v3 quotas: 1,000,000 quota units/min per project, 325,000/min per user, 400,000,000 units/day free threshold, 1 TB/day project egress. Per-method costs: `files.get` = 5 units, `files.list` = 100, `files.download` = 200, `files.update` = 50. A 60-image site costs 60×200 + 100 = 12,100 units per cold build — 0.003% of the daily free threshold. Also: `files.export` output is capped at 10 MB.

Google Docs gained native Markdown export on 2024-07-16 (Rapid) / 2024-07-31 (Scheduled) for ALL account types including personal. `text/markdown` is a supported `files.export` MIME type, and `https://docs.google.com/document/d/{ID}/export?format=markdown` works for link-shared docs. This is dramatically better than HTML export, which emits inline styles, generated `c1`/`c3`/`c8` classes, empty `<span>` wrappers and `<b>` instead of `<strong>`. GOTCHA: images inside a Doc come out of Markdown export as base64 `data:` URIs that render broken; use `application/zip` (Web Page HTML, zipped) instead, which emits the HTML plus real image files in an `images/` folder.

Apps Script has a hard gotcha for the publish trigger: the SIMPLE `onEdit(e)` trigger cannot call `UrlFetchApp` — it runs without authorization. You must create an INSTALLABLE edit trigger (via `ScriptApp.newTrigger('...').forSpreadsheet(ss).onEdit().create()`). Apps Script quotas: UrlFetch 20,000/day (consumer gmail.com) vs 100,000/day (Workspace — iith.ac.in is Workspace); trigger total runtime 90 min/day consumer vs 6 hr/day Workspace; 6 min max per execution.

Vercel Hobby is legally unusable for this project if Divyansh is paid. Verified from Vercel's own fair-use page: "Hobby teams are restricted to non-commercial personal use only... Commercial usage is defined as any Deployment that is used for the purpose of financial gain of ANYONE involved in ANY part of the production of the project, including a paid employee or consultant writing the code," with the explicit example "Receiving payment to create, update, or host the site." Donations also count. Separately: "Vercel does not support connecting a project on your Hobby team to Git repositories owned by Git organizations."

Real platform numbers (from official docs): Vercel Hobby = 100 deployments/day, 100 builds/hour, 45-min build cap, 1 concurrent build, 5 deploy hooks/project, deploy-hook triggers capped at 60/hour/project, 2 build vCPU / 8 GB, fair-use 100 GB transfer + 5K image transformations/month. Cloudflare Pages Free = 500 builds/month, 1 concurrent build, 20-min build timeout, 20,000 files/site, 25 MiB max single asset, 100 custom domains, UNLIMITED bandwidth, commercial use allowed. Cloudflare Pages is the correct host here.

Vercel deploy hooks accept GET as well as POST (`curl -X POST https://api.vercel.com/v1/integrations/deploy/prj_XXX/YYY`), require no auth header, and duplicate triggers cancel the previous build. Netlify build hooks are `https://api.netlify.com/build_hooks/{id}` and accept `?trigger_title=...&trigger_branch=...&clear_cache=true` plus a custom body exposed to the build as `$INCOMING_HOOK_BODY`. Because GET works, a deploy-hook URL pasted into a Doc or Sheet can be fired by a link-prefetcher — treat it strictly as a secret and prefer GitHub `repository_dispatch` with a scoped token.

GitHub Actions `schedule` is officially best-effort: minimum interval 5 minutes, and GitHub's own docs say "The schedule event can be delayed during periods of high loads of GitHub Actions workflow runs. High load times include the start of every hour. If the load is sufficiently high enough, some queued jobs may be dropped." Plus: "In a public repository, scheduled workflows are automatically disabled when no repository activity has occurred in 60 days" — and only new commits reset that timer, not issues/releases/tags. Cron alone is not a publish mechanism; it is only a safety net. Actions minutes are unlimited-free on public repos, 2,000/month on free private repos, then $0.006/min for Linux 2-core.

CMS repo health, pulled live from the GitHub API on 2026-09-04: sveltia/sveltia-cms = 2,787 stars, MIT, latest release v0.205.3 published 2026-09-04 (same day), 58 open issues — but still 0.x, and it is explicitly "a personal project of an experienced UX engineer" (Kohei Yoshino), i.e. bus-factor 1. decaporg/decap-cms = 19,344 stars, MIT, decap-cms@3.16.0 on 2026-08-31, 589 open issues — less dead than its reputation suggests. Thinkmill/keystatic = 2,348 stars, MIT, last push 2026-08-26, zero GitHub releases (ships via npm/changesets). tinacms/tinacms = 13,773 stars, Apache-2.0, active.

The Netlify Identity scare resolved in Decap's favour: Netlify announced deprecation in Feb 2025, then reversed on 2026-02-19 — "Netlify Identity will continue as a supported authentication option on Netlify... No required migrations." Git Gateway's status is murkier and community threads still recommend moving off it to direct GitHub OAuth, DecapBridge, or Auth0. For our purposes this is moot: Sveltia and Pages CMS authenticate directly against the GitHub API and need neither Identity nor Git Gateway.

Competitor image URLs are a trap for static sites. Notion API image URLs are AWS S3 signed links valid for ONE HOUR (rate limit: avg 3 req/s per connection, 429 with a `Retry-After` header, 1,000 blocks / 500 KB per request, 2,000 chars per rich-text field). Airtable attachment download URLs on `airtableusercontent.com` are guaranteed only "at least 2 hours" (rate limit 5 req/s per base; Free plan caps 1,000 records per base and 5 editors per workspace). Both mandate the same build-time download-and-commit pipeline as Drive, so neither removes work — they only add a vendor.

Pricing at our scale (one professor + maybe one student editor): Google Sheets/Docs/Drive = $0 (already owned via iith.ac.in Workspace). Sveltia/Decap/Keystatic/Pages CMS = $0, MIT-licensed, self-hosted. TinaCMS free = 2 users only, then $24/mo. Sanity free = 20 seats / 10,000 docs / 2 public datasets / 1M CDN requests / 100 GB bandwidth, then $15/seat/mo. Contentful free = 10 users / 100K API calls / 50 GB CDN, then a $300/mo cliff to Lite. Airtable free = 1,000 records/base (a publication list will hit this in ~15 years; the 5-editor cap never binds).

Astro's Content Layer API is a near-perfect fit: a custom `Loader` is `{ name, load(context), schema }` where `context` gives you `store`, `meta`, `logger`, `parseData()`, `generateDigest()` and `renderMarkdown()`. `parseData()` runs the Zod schema and Astro "will provide a helpful error" on violation, failing the build. `generateDigest()` + `store.set({id, data, digest})` gives free incremental caching so unchanged rows don't churn. Astro also uses sharp as its default image service and optimises REMOTE images at build time for prerendered pages, provided the host is allow-listed in `image.domains` / `image.remotePatterns`.

Zod 4 ships exactly the human-readable error surface this needs: `z.prettifyError(err)` returns a multi-line string like `✖ Invalid input: expected string, received number\n  → at username`, alongside `z.treeifyError()` (nested, mirrors the schema) and `z.flattenError()` (shallow). `prettifyError` is explicitly designed for logs — it is what should be written into the CI log AND back into the professor's spreadsheet.

gviz CSV output pads every row out to the sheet's full allocated column count — the Google sample sheet returned 6 real headers followed by 16 empty `""` columns. Any CSV-based parser must trim trailing empty-header columns or the schema will see phantom fields.
recommendations: PRIMARY RECOMMENDATION — a Google-only content plane with a Git-backed build. Google Sheets holds every tabular collection (publications, people, alumni, news, teaching, awards). Google Docs holds every long-form page (bio, research statement, RAFT narrative) and every blog post — one Doc per item, its link pasted into a `pages` / `blog` tab. Google Drive holds every image in one folder. This is ONE mental model for the professor: 'everything lives in my Drive.' Do not make him learn a second tool for the blog; that is where these projects die.

Read the sheet with the OFFICIAL Sheets API v4 `spreadsheets.values.batchGet`, authenticated by a SERVICE ACCOUNT, in a single request for all tabs. Do NOT use gviz as the primary path — it returns HTTP 200 + `status:"ok"` and silently serves the FIRST sheet when a tab name is wrong, which converts a typo into silently-wrong published content. batchGet returns a hard 400 naming the bad range. Use `valueRenderOption=UNFORMATTED_VALUE` plus `dateTimeRenderOption=FORMATTED_STRING` so numbers stay numbers and dates stay readable.

Use a service account, not OAuth and not an API key. OAuth would drag you into Google's SENSITIVE (`spreadsheets.readonly`) and RESTRICTED (`drive.readonly`) scope verification, including a security assessment. A service account needs no consent screen. Store the JSON key base64-encoded in a single CI secret (`GOOGLE_SA_KEY_B64`) to avoid the classic `\n`-mangling of the private key, and share the Sheet + image folder to the service-account email as Viewer only.

Build the image pipeline as Drive-folder → build-time download → sharp → AVIF+WebP+fallback → content-hashed filename → committed cache. The professor pastes ANY Drive link shape into a Sheet cell; extract the ID with `/(?:\/file\/d\/|\/document\/d\/|\/folders\/|[?&]id=)([A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,})/` (verified against all five link shapes Drive produces) and also accept a bare ID. Key the cache on `fileId + modifiedTime` from `files.get?fields=id,name,mimeType,modifiedTime,md5Checksum` (5 quota units) so unchanged images are never re-downloaded — this is what keeps you clear of `downloadQuotaExceeded`.

NEVER hot-link `drive.google.com/thumbnail` or `lh3.googleusercontent.com` from the live site. Both are undocumented, both 429 under load, and `uc?export=view` already died once in January 2024 taking every Drive-backed GitHub Pages site with it. Serve only self-hosted, hashed, immutable files with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`.

For prose, prefer Drive API `files.export` with `mimeType=application/zip` (Web Page HTML, zipped) over `text/markdown`. Markdown export inlines images as base64 `data:` URIs that render broken; the zip gives you clean-ish HTML plus real image binaries in `images/`. Then sanitise the HTML through rehype (strip `style`, strip generated `c1`/`c3` classes, promote `<b>`→`<strong>`, `<i>`→`<em>`, rewrite image `src` into the same sharp pipeline) rather than trusting Google's markup. Keep `text/markdown` as the path for image-free docs, where it is genuinely clean.

Use a Sheet cell for prose only under ~500 characters (abstracts, one-line bios, news blurbs). Above that, switch to a Doc. The line is not technical, it is editorial: a Sheet cell has no headings, no links, no paragraph structure, and no revision-history granularity. Give the Sheet a `body_doc_url` column that, when non-empty, overrides a short `body` column — so short items stay in one place and long items graduate to a Doc without a schema change.

PUBLISH TRIGGER — use all three layers, in this order. (1) PRIMARY: an Apps Script custom menu item `🚀 Publish site` added in `onOpen()`, which POSTs to a GitHub `repository_dispatch` (scoped fine-grained PAT, not a bare deploy hook) and immediately shows `SpreadsheetApp.getActive().toast('Publishing… the site updates in about 3 minutes')`. Explicit, intentional, zero surprise. (2) SAFETY NET: a `schedule: cron` nightly rebuild — but note GitHub explicitly drops queued scheduled jobs under load and auto-disables cron on public repos after 60 days of no commits, so always pair it with `workflow_dispatch`. (3) NEVER use a bare installable `onEdit` trigger as the primary — it fires on every keystroke, will burn the 90-min/day (consumer) or 6-hr/day (Workspace) trigger runtime budget, and cannot use `UrlFetchApp` at all from a SIMPLE trigger.

Close the feedback loop by writing the build result BACK into the professor's own spreadsheet. Give the workbook a `_Publish Log` tab, grant the service account Editor on that one sheet (protect every other tab), and have the workflow append a row on both success and failure: timestamp, status, and on failure the `z.prettifyError()` string. He then sees `2026-09-04 14:03 | ❌ FAILED | Publications row 12: "year" must be a number, got "forthcoming"` in the tool he is already looking at. Back this with GitHub's native failure email to Divyansh. This single feature is the difference between a site he maintains and a site he abandons.

Validate with Zod at the row level and fail the build loudly. Never coerce silently. Check header presence explicitly BEFORE parsing rows (`assertHeaders(actual, expected)`) so a deleted or renamed column produces `Missing column "year" in tab "Publications". Found: title, authors, venue, yr` rather than 40 confusing per-row errors. Report ALL failing rows in one pass with the human-readable spreadsheet row number (`index + 2`, accounting for the header), not just the first failure — a non-technical editor must not have to iterate one error per build.

Rely on atomic deploys as the real safety net: on Cloudflare Pages, Netlify and Vercel a failed build simply does not replace the live deployment. Say this to the professor in plain words: 'If you make a mistake, the website does not break. It just keeps showing the last good version, and you get an email telling you what to fix.' That sentence removes most of the fear that makes non-technical owners stop editing.

HOST ON CLOUDFLARE PAGES, not Vercel Hobby. If Divyansh is paid anything for this work, Vercel's fair-use policy explicitly classifies the deployment as commercial ("Receiving payment to create, update, or host the site") and Hobby forbids it — that is a real account-suspension risk on a professor's public site. Cloudflare Pages Free permits commercial use, gives unlimited bandwidth, 500 builds/month and 100 custom domains. Build in GitHub Actions (unlimited free on a public repo) and deploy with `wrangler pages deploy` for full control over Node version, secrets and the image cache.

Engineer the spreadsheet itself as a UI, not a database dump. Per tab: freeze row 1 (View → Freeze → 1 row); bold + fill the header; protect the header range (Data → Protect sheets and ranges → row 1, 'Only you' or warning-only); add Data Validation dropdowns for every enum column (`type`: journal/conference/preprint; `status`: draft/published); add a checkbox column for `featured`; set a date-format on date columns. Add a `README` tab as the first tab explaining each column in one sentence and showing one filled-in EXAMPLE ROW, kept as row 2 and skipped by the build via a leading `#` in the id column.

Steal Mark Hansen's foreign-key trick for cross-tab references — since Sheets has no referential integrity, add a validation column with `=IF(ISBLANK(F3),,IF(ISNA(FILTER(People!B:B,People!B:B=F3)),"❌","✅"))`. The professor sees a red ❌ next to a misspelled student name the instant he types it, in-sheet, before the build ever runs. Client-side validation always beats build-time validation for non-technical editors.

Use Astro with a custom Content Layer loader rather than a hand-rolled prebuild script. The `{ name, load({ store, parseData, generateDigest, logger }), schema }` contract gives you Zod validation, digest-based incremental caching and proper build-log integration for free, and `renderMarkdown()` handles the Docs prose. It also means the content is typed end-to-end, so a renamed column becomes a TypeScript error in the templates too, not just a runtime one.

ON THE HYBRID QUESTION — recommend AGAINST a second CMS at launch, but architect for it. Adding Sveltia/Keystatic for the blog means a second login, a second mental model and a second thing to explain, for a professor whose stated preference is Google tools. Instead: keep Docs-as-blog, but write every fetched Doc to `content/blog/{slug}.md` and COMMIT it. The repo then already contains exactly the Markdown-with-frontmatter tree that Sveltia CMS or Keystatic expects. If in six months he wants live preview or a student wants to write posts, you point Sveltia at `content/blog/` and it works on day one with zero migration. That is the cheapest possible option on the future.

PLAN FOR DIVYANSH DISAPPEARING — this is a first-class requirement, not an afterthought. Commit the fetched JSON and Markdown into the repo (not just the built HTML) so the content is portable with zero Google access. Write `docs/HANDOVER.md` covering: where the Sheet is, where the service-account key lives and how to rotate it, how to trigger a build by hand, and how to run the site locally. Add a `pnpm run eject` script that dumps every collection to plain Markdown + frontmatter. Pin exact dependency versions and add a Renovate config. Record one 10-minute screen capture of the professor's actual publish workflow. A site whose content is Markdown in Git and whose source of truth is the professor's own Google Sheet survives any developer leaving; one that depends on a bespoke undocumented pipeline does not.

Do NOT use Notion or Airtable here. Both add a vendor, neither is a tool the professor already uses, and both have MORE hostile asset stories than Drive: Notion's image URLs expire in 1 hour and Airtable's in ~2, so you still build the same download-and-commit pipeline you would have built for Drive. Airtable's 1,000-records-per-base free cap also puts a clock on a publication list. The only genuine reason to pick them would be relational integrity, which the ✅/❌ FILTER formula gives us in Sheets for free.
pitfalls: gviz's silent fallback is the trap that will actually bite this project: a renamed or misspelled tab returns HTTP 200 with `status:"ok"` and serves the FIRST sheet instead. The build goes green and publishes the wrong data. Verified live — the response signature for `sheet=NoSuchTab` was byte-identical to the no-sheet-param request. Use the official API, which 400s on a bad range.

Hot-linking `drive.google.com/thumbnail` or `lh3.googleusercontent.com` in production. `uc?export=view` already died once in January 2024 and took every Drive-backed GitHub Pages site with it; the thumbnail endpoint is just a 302 to an undocumented lh3 URL that 429s under load. This will work perfectly in testing and fail on the day the site gets posted to a conference Slack.

Hitting `downloadQuotaExceeded` (403, `usageLimits`, ~10–30 min lockout, service accounts not exempt) by re-downloading every image on every build. Cache on `fileId + modifiedTime` or a busy editing day locks you out mid-deploy.

Deploying to Vercel Hobby if Divyansh is paid. Vercel's own wording — "financial gain of anyone involved in any part of the production... including a paid employee or consultant writing the code" and "Receiving payment to create, update, or host the site" — makes this a policy violation with real suspension risk. Donations count too, which matters if a lab donate button ever appears.

Reaching for OAuth instead of a service account. `spreadsheets.readonly` is a SENSITIVE scope needing Google app verification; `drive.readonly` is RESTRICTED, needing verification plus a third-party security assessment. Weeks of process for zero benefit, plus refresh tokens that silently rot in CI.

Using the "Publish to web" 2PACX CSV URL as a build source. Google caches it; the professor edits, publishes, sees no change, edits again, loses trust in the whole system. `/export?format=csv` and `/gviz/tq` both return `cache-control: no-cache, no-store` (verified) — 2PACX does not.

Relying on GitHub Actions `schedule` cron as the publish mechanism. GitHub's own docs: "The schedule event can be delayed during periods of high loads... some queued jobs may be dropped," and public-repo cron auto-disables after 60 days with no COMMITS (issues, releases and tags do not reset the timer). A site that publishes only on cron will one day just stop.

Wiring a simple `onEdit(e)` trigger to the deploy webhook. Simple triggers cannot call `UrlFetchApp` at all, and even the installable version fires on every keystroke — it will burn the 90-min/day (consumer) or 6-hr/day (Workspace) trigger runtime budget and hammer the 60-triggers/hour deploy-hook cap.

Pasting a Vercel or Netlify deploy-hook URL somewhere convenient (a Doc, a Sheet cell, a bookmark). Vercel deploy hooks accept GET with no auth header, so any link-prefetcher, scanner or email-safety-scan can redeploy the site. Use `repository_dispatch` with a scoped PAT held in Apps Script Script Properties.

Parsing sheet rows by column INDEX. The professor will reorder columns — it is the single most natural thing to do in a spreadsheet. Always key by header name, and assert the header set before parsing any rows.

Forgetting to trim trailing empty columns from gviz/CSV output. Sheets pads every row to the tab's allocated column count — the 6-column sample returned 6 real headers plus 16 empty ones, which then become 16 phantom schema fields.
Exporting a Doc containing images as `text/markdown`. Images come out as base64 `data:` URIs that render broken. Use `application/zip` (HTML + real image files) for any doc with images.

Shipping Google's HTML export raw. It carries inline styles, generated `c1`/`c3`/`c8` classes, empty spans, `<b>` instead of `<strong>`, AND rewrites every external link through `google.com/url?q=` — which leaks referrers from the professor's site to Google on every outbound click.

Reporting only the FIRST validation error. A non-technical editor who has to run the build once per mistake across eight bad rows will give up on the fourth. Collect and report every problem in one pass, with real spreadsheet row numbers (`index + 2`), not array indices.

Choosing Notion or Airtable expecting to skip the image pipeline. Notion's image URLs expire in 1 hour and Airtable's in ~2 — you build exactly the same download-and-commit pipeline as Drive, and pay a vendor for the privilege.

Committing raw Drive originals to git. A few dozen 8 MP phone photos bloat the repo permanently, and git history never forgets. Commit only the derived, resized outputs; restore originals via `actions/cache`.

Betting the blog on Sveltia CMS today. It is genuinely the best-designed option in the Git-CMS space and shipped v0.205.3 the day I checked — but it is still 0.x and explicitly "a personal project of an experienced UX engineer." Bus-factor 1 on a site meant to outlive the developer. Keeping the content as plain Markdown in the repo means Sveltia stays an optional, swappable UI layer rather than a dependency.

Silently coercing bad data instead of failing. `z.coerce.number()` on "forthcoming" yields NaN, which renders as a blank year on a live publication list — a wrong site is far worse than a failed build that keeps the previous good version up.

exemplars.name: Mark Hansen — independent (Wellington, NZ) — "Run a website off a Google Sheets Database, with Hugo"
exemplars.what_works: The most honest write-up of this exact architecture from someone who shipped it. He explicitly ABANDONED the official Sheets API for gviz because of "excessive boilerplate — API keys, typed struct mapping, and fragile column-index dependencies," then hit the two failure modes that matter: (a) Sheets has no referential integrity, so cross-tab references silently break; (b) user-entered strings become file paths, so a malicious/clumsy value like `../../../etc/passwd` escapes the content dir — he guards it with `os.path.commonprefix()`. Build is `git submodule update --init --recursive && jupyter nbconvert --execute Generate.ipynb && hugo` on Netlify.
exemplars.steal_this: The in-sheet foreign-key validation column: `=IF(ISBLANK(F3),,IF(ISNA(FILTER(Formats!B:B,Formats!B:B=F3)),"❌","✅"))`. It puts a red ❌ next to a mistyped cross-reference the instant the professor types it — client-side, in his own spreadsheet, before any build runs. Adapt it so the People tab validates student names referenced from Publications. Client-side validation beats build-time validation for non-technical editors every single time. Also steal the path-traversal guard when turning sheet values into filenames.

exemplars.name: Harry Cresswell — independent (UK) — "Generate pages from Google Sheets using Hugo's Content Adapters"
exemplars.what_works: Documents the single most important caching gotcha with hard specifics: "Google caches requests to Sheets. This means that if we keep making requests to the same URL, then any updates made to the sheet won't necessarily be visible." His fix is a cache-buster — a SHA256 of the current timestamp appended to the published-to-web URL. He also shows a clean loader shape: `resources.GetRemote` → `transform.Unmarshal` → `range after 1 $data` (skipping the header row) → `.AddPage`, generating pages purely in memory with no Markdown files written.
exemplars.steal_this: Two things. First, the negative lesson: he needs a cache-buster only because he used the 2PACX published-to-web URL — I verified that `/export?format=csv` and `/gviz/tq` return `cache-control: no-cache, no-store, max-age=0, must-revalidate`, so choosing the right endpoint removes the problem instead of working around it. Second, the positive: `range after 1 $data` as the header-skip idiom maps directly onto our `rowsToObjects()` — and his "no files written" approach is exactly what Astro's Content Layer `store.set()` does natively, which is why Astro is the better host for this pattern than Hugo.

exemplars.name: Pascal Michaillat — UC Santa Cruz (Economics) — minimalist Hugo academic template
exemplars.what_works: A genuinely restrained academic site from a working professor, and a useful counter-model. Content is one Markdown file per item across `papers/`, `courses/`, `data/`, `books/`, with Hugo archetypes so `hugo new papers/foo.md` scaffolds the frontmatter. The stated aesthetic — "color scheme, font, spacing, and general appearance streamlined and as minimalist as possible," mostly grayscale with a single slate blue reserved for interactive elements — is exactly the editorial register Dr. Regonda's brief asks for, and it proves the look does not require a heavy CMS. Cover images are spec'd at a fixed 1280×720 so lists and social cards stay uniform.
exemplars.steal_this: The one-file-per-item content model as our COMMITTED OUTPUT format. Our build should write `content/publications/{slug}.md` and `content/blog/{slug}.md` in exactly this shape. That gives three wins at once: the repo stays human-readable and portable if Google or the pipeline ever dies; a future developer sees a completely conventional Hugo/Astro content tree; and pointing Sveltia CMS or Keystatic at `content/blog/` later requires zero migration. Also steal the fixed 1280×720 cover-image contract — enforce it in the Zod schema so the professor cannot break card layouts by pasting a portrait phone photo.

exemplars.name: Ben Borgers — opensheet (hosted Google Sheets → JSON proxy)
exemplars.what_works: The cleanest possible ergonomics for the read step, and worth studying even though we won't depend on it. `https://opensheet.elk.sh/{spreadsheet_id}/{tab_name_or_index}` returns a plain JSON array of objects keyed by the header row — verified live, with `access-control-allow-origin: *` and `cache-control: public, max-age=59, s-maxage=59` behind Cloudflare. Tabs are addressable by NAME or by 1-based index, and `?raw=true` switches from Google-formatted display values to underlying values. Requirements are honest and minimal: a header row, and link-sharing on.
exemplars.steal_this: Its output contract, reimplemented locally: an array of objects keyed by trimmed header names, one object per row. That is the shape our `rowsToObjects()` should produce, and it makes the Zod schemas read like plain records. Also steal the `?raw=true` distinction — expose `valueRenderOption` in our loader so date and number columns can be read UNFORMATTED (real numbers) while text stays FORMATTED. What we must NOT steal is the dependency itself: a free single-maintainer proxy with a ~60s cache and no SLA sitting in the critical path of a professor's site is exactly the kind of quiet third-party risk this project should avoid.

exemplars.name: Pages CMS — open-source Git-backed CMS (pagescms.org)
exemplars.what_works: The lowest-friction Git CMS I verified: MIT-licensed, 100% free in both hosted (app.pagescms.org) and self-hosted forms, deployable to Vercel at no cost, and it edits content directly in a GitHub repo with no database, API or backend. Critically for our user, collaborators can be invited BY EMAIL without needing their own accounts, and it ships a real media manager with drag-and-drop and multi-file upload.
exemplars.steal_this: Keep it in the back pocket as the day-two escape hatch, and let it dictate our on-disk format now. Because it reads ordinary YAML-frontmatter Markdown from a repo, writing our fetched Docs to `content/blog/{slug}.md` means Pages CMS (or Sveltia, or Keystatic) can be bolted on later with a config file and zero content migration. The email-invite flow is also the specific feature that would matter if a RAFT student ever needs to post news without being given a GitHub account — worth noting in HANDOVER.md as the pre-vetted upgrade path rather than something to build now.
